headline: US September consumer prices land today with consensus at 3.6 to 3.7 percent on the year, the last inflation reading before the Oct 27 to 28 Fed meeting, and it arrives with WTI at 95.28 dollars and the 10 year Treasury yield at 5.217 percent, while India went the other way as HCLTech earnings drove the Nifty up 1.60 percent to 22,721.95 and the Nifty IT index to its best session in more than 17 months.

summary.us: The S&P 500 closed Tuesday at 7,805.45, down 0.02 percent, the Nasdaq Composite at 27,204.38, down 0.15 percent, and the Dow at 51,670.10, down 0.35 percent, as mixed bank results and a second day of memory chip selling offset gains elsewhere. JPMorgan earned 5.57 dollars a share against a consensus near 5.90 dollars on a 658 million dollar securities loss and fell 0.86 percent, Citigroup beat at 2.85 dollars but dropped 5.60 percent after markets revenue fell 13 percent from the prior quarter and management guided to a further 20 percent decline, Goldman Sachs beat at 17.01 dollars against 12.86 dollars expected on a 72 percent jump in equities revenue, Wells Fargo lost 3.10 percent, Johnson & Johnson fell 5.73 percent after MedTech sales rose only 2.5 percent to 8.6 billion dollars for a second straight miss, Micron lost 3.62 percent, and the 10 year yield eased to 5.217 percent after New York Fed President John Williams said no hikes look necessary in 2027.
summary.india: The Nifty closed Tuesday at 22,721.95, up 1.60 percent, and Bank Nifty at 55,481.05, up 1.03 percent, led by HCLTech's September quarter net profit rise of about 21 percent to 5,132 crore rupees, an EBIT margin of 18.2 percent against 17.4 percent a year earlier, record deal bookings of 3.3 billion dollars and FY27 constant currency guidance narrowed to 2.5 to 4 percent from 1 to 4 percent, which sent HCLTECH up 8.42 percent, TCS 6.79 percent, Tech Mahindra 4.93 percent, Wipro 4.45 percent and Infosys 4.13 percent in sympathy for the Nifty IT index's best day in more than 17 months. India VIX fell 7.41 percent to 14.12, foreign investors sold a net 1,305 crore rupees against 2,439 crore rupees of domestic buying on a thirteenth straight selling day, and the rupee held near a one month peak after the RBI opened a special dollar window for three state refiners and introduced a foreign exchange risk reserve requirement on transactions above 2 million dollars.
summary.global: Tuesday's Asian session carried the CXMT memory selloff, with the Kospi down 5.46 percent to 6,035.35 after touching 5,914.35 and the Nikkei 225 down 1.82 percent to 67,777.52, while the Hang Seng recovered 0.30 percent to 24,345.22; Europe slipped with the Stoxx 600 down 0.10 percent to 635.01, the FTSE 100 off 0.06 percent, the DAX off 0.07 percent, ASML down 4.2 percent ahead of results and LVMH reporting Fashion and Leather Goods revenue down 5 percent organic. Early Wednesday brought a bounce, with the Kospi up 0.83 percent, the Nikkei up 0.36 percent and Samsung Electronics up 1.62 percent, while the dollar index fell 0.40 percent to 102.17 on the Williams comments and Brent held near 105 to 107 dollars after Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and fresh tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz.

weekly.narrative: The week turned on the long end of the Treasury curve, where yields pushed to multi year highs midweek and the 30 year auction cleared at 5.618 percent, the highest since August 2000, before solid demand cooled the move and let the S&P 500 finish 1.15 percent higher and the Nasdaq 0.64 percent higher despite a Thursday air pocket when the Financial Times reported OpenAI annualized revenue about 20 billion dollars below the figure circulated to investors. India spent the week absorbing the RBI's first rate hike since February 2023, a 25 basis point move to 5.50 percent on Oct 7 paired with a hawkish calibrated tightening stance and an FY27 CPI forecast lifted to 5.2 percent, which left the Nifty up only 0.44 percent while Bank Nifty gained 1.48 percent and foreign investors kept selling, including a 12,944 crore rupee outflow on Oct 8. Metals were the cleanest trade, with copper up 3.37 percent on the Centinela strike in Chile and Chinese restocking, and silver and gold adding 1.89 and 1.39 percent as real yields retreated into Friday. Crypto went the other way, bitcoin down 2.58 percent and ether down 7.34 percent on the week, pressured by high oil costs, rate hike expectations and Middle East risk. Next week brings the first real test of earnings season, with JPMorgan and Citigroup on Oct 13 and Bank of America on Oct 14, alongside US September CPI on Oct 14 that the street expects at 3.6 percent on the year, India September CPI, and TSMC results on Oct 15.
